The Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, and Edo State Governor Senator Monday Okpebholo have set a target of 2.5 million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 16 January 2027 presidential election.
The duo made the declaration in Benin City, Edo State, during the inauguration of the state chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, established to mobilise grassroots support for Tinubu’s re-election.
President Tinubu is the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate in the election.
Tompolo, represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, Kestin Pondi, also donated 25 campaign vehicles equipped with loudspeakers, generators and amplifiers to facilitate the mobilisation campaign across the state.
He said the vehicles would be deployed to take the message of Tinubu’s administration to households, markets, churches and communities, urging residents to support the president for another four years.
He said although Nigerians were experiencing economic difficulties, the reforms introduced by Mr Tinubu were beginning to yield results, adding that the benefits would gradually extend to small businesses and ordinary citizens.
According to him, the president needs another four years to consolidate the foundation his administration has already laid.

“Big businesses are already benefiting from the reforms. In no distant time, the benefits will get to small businesses,” he said.
Tompolo urged members of the movement to engage their neighbours, relatives and community members, explaining the administration’s policies and persuading them to vote for Mr Tinubu.
Also speaking, Mr Okpebholo said the 2.5 million-vote target was a commitment to Mr Tinubu, stressing that the state would work to deliver promised votes.
He described Tompolo as a great leader for establishing a grassroots political mobilisation platform, adding that the initiative would strengthen support for Tinubu’s continuity in office.
The governor called on party members and supporters to take the campaign to individual homes and communities to ensure that the target was achieved.
Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Asuku, said the initiative was established to mobilise Nigerians for Mr Tinubu’s re-election, insisting that the president deserved another four years to consolidate his reforms.
Mr Asuku argued that the administration had improved allocations to states and local governments, strengthened their financial capacity and enabled state governments to meet salary and pension obligations while executing development projects.
Also speaking, the Edo State APC Chairman, Jarrett Tenebe, said the state party leadership was committed to delivering the votes the President promised.
Mr Tenebe cited Mr Tinubu’s support for the emergence of a South-south son as senate president and other appointments given to people from the region as reasons for the zone to reciprocate through massive electoral support.
He expressed confidence that the inauguration of the movement would strengthen the party’s grassroots mobilisation and help Edo State achieve the 2.5 million votes target.
